title: Verifier architecture reconciliation
canonical_definition: Inventory all existing verifier, policy, selector, attestation and signed-verdict components. Freeze canonical ownership and authority boundaries.

existing_components.role: worker admission composition over capability attestation

identity_and_lifecycle.requirement: Register, activate, suspend, rotate and retire verifier identities without granting unrelated authority.
identity_and_lifecycle.canonical_future_surface: ComputeVerifierRegistry420 or equivalently named authorized implementation
identity_and_lifecycle.non_duplicative_rule: Do not reinterpret ComputeVerifierIndependencePolicy420 identities as the verifier lifecycle registry.

classes_and_capabilities.requirement: Support independently typed verifier classes and workload capabilities.
classes_and_capabilities.rule: Class/capability eligibility is distinct from appointment, identity attestation, correctness proof and settlement.

verification_policy.requirement: Bind jobs to exact versioned verification policies before execution.
verification_policy.rule: Accepted profile/policy semantics are immutable for an accepted job; publication is not a verdict.

signed_verdicts.rule: Authentication proves decision provenance, not correctness by itself.

independent_selection.rule: Verifier cannot self-appoint; selector cannot grant capability or publish profiles; attestor cannot appoint.

challenge_and_appeal.rule: Challenges/appeals do not rewrite immutable original verdicts and do not themselves move funds.

authority_boundaries: Verifier identity or verification capability grants no Vault custody, arbitrary withdrawal, beneficiary redirection, settlement execution, worker lifecycle, validator, bridge, governance, or arbitrary-wallet authority.
A signed verdict proves provenance/authentication only; correctness requires the bound verification method/profile.
A verification PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE decision is evidence under a bound policy and does not itself transfer funds.
Settlement beneficiary and amount derive from canonical accepted economic state, never a verifier argument.
Verifier selector, identity attestor, profile/policy publisher, verifier, dispute reviewer, worker, payer and settlement authority remain separable roles.
Policy publication or profile approval does not appoint a verifier and cannot retroactively rewrite accepted-job verification semantics.
Worker/resource reputation or 420Trust evidence cannot substitute for independent correctness verification where independence is required.
Raw private workload/evidence bytes are not required canonical plaintext; on-chain state stores bounded commitments/provenance.
Suspension or revocation may block new verification activity but must not silently rewrite historical decisions or confiscate independently earned valid entitlements.
Emergency/governance authority cannot fabricate verification outcomes or redirect balances.
Non-AI workloads remain first-class; verifier architecture cannot require 420AI participation.

deployment_publication.note: CMP-1.4.0 freezes architecture only. No verifier deployment/address/runtime-hash/publication evidence is fabricated.

exit_criteria: All existing verifier/policy/selector/attestation/signed-verdict components are inventoried and dispositioned.

Canonical ownership for verifier identity/lifecycle, classes/capabilities, policy, verdicts, selection, quorum, adapters, scientific verification, disputes, qualification, release and closeout is frozen to CMP-1.4.1 through CMP-1.4.12.
Authority separation is explicit and consistent with frozen ComputeMarket invariants.
Legacy/test-only and bounded-profile components are not promoted into the canonical general verifier registry.
Retained tests/docs required by later CMP-1.4 work are identified.
Architecture freeze is mechanically verified and qualified on the exact final head.

planned_missing_surfaces.disposition: target architecture name only; later CMP-1.4 implementation must reconcile router responsibilities without treating the name as existing code or deployment.
